body:
Coordinator lesson (Termal::Fable2, 2026-11-24). Seen on w-cf04 R6, and on w-56f3 evaluations 4 and 5.

Acceptance evaluators read each criterion and its stated limits literally, and they test edge cases against the exact words. A "file it, it's inside the limit" ruling is overturned whenever the case is only arguably inside the limit. Example: the limit said "if the host's look leaves the record pending for a reason ...", and the evaluator read "the host's look" as the CURRENT look, so a release on a stale mirror reason failed.

Rules for rulings:
(1) Before filing a Medium as "inside the stated limit", check that the limit's exact words cover it with no interpretation. If it takes an argument, fix it, or reword the limit explicitly with concurrence.
(2) Prefer designs that make the authoritative state single and current, for example an in-memory latest look for every outcome, over fallbacks to persisted copies that can go stale.
(3) When a criterion promises the physically impossible, such as killing a process in uninterruptible sleep, correct it explicitly with a tracked item. Never leave the evaluator to discover it.

Addendum (w-56f3 evaluation d34df0a9, 2026-11-25): a stated limit is read as a PROHIBITION, not as an exemption. The limit "X is not followed further; its settlement reaches only the owner" failed a candidate that DID follow X when a record was in flight, even though following it was strictly more helpful. So when a criterion states a limit, the code must do exactly what the limit says, no more and no less. Also make sure every case a limit names is distinguishable at runtime, for example by splitting a shared reason code, so that no case covered elsewhere (such as removal) is swept into the limit by accident.
